brief:
British-led sanctions targeting Israeli settlement expansion in the West Bank could backfire by strengthening right-wing parties ahead of elections, according to analysts and diplomatic sources cited by Al-Monitor. The punitive measures risk being portrayed as foreign interference, potentially rallying nationalist voters around hardline candidates who oppose international pressure.

The sanctions were designed to discourage settlement growth, but critics warn they may have the opposite political effect. Analysts suggest the measures could consolidate support for the Israeli right by framing sanctions as an external threat rather than a consequence of settlement policy.

title: Sanctions on settlements may embolden Israeli right before vote
